channel.description: Recent content in Termorq CLI on Termorq

item.title: Run a collection
item.description:
Running collections as runbooks is a Pro feature. Free builds can still list collections with termorq-cli list and inspect them with termorq-cli show. The available commands follow the edition compiled into termorq-cli; the CLI has no edition flag or runtime switch.

termorq-cli runs a saved collection without opening Termorq. It uses the same HTTP calls, variables, response checks, and captures as the app. Version 0.20.0 prints termorq-cli 0.20.0.

The screenshots on this page are the real binary, taken against a sample workspace at /tmp/acme-apis. That workspace points Users API at mock://users, the app’s offline demo host, so nothing left the machine. A secret named in the prompt is shown as …. The value never appears in the output.

item.title: Secrets and termorq-cli
item.description:
termorq-cli will not start a run that needs a secret it cannot find, and it scrubs every secret it does find from the text, JSON, YAML, and JUnit it writes. This page is the CLI. The app’s keychain, export files, and workspace guard get their own chapter later.

Where the secret comes from link

For each connection a step will call, termorq-cli looks in this order:

  1. The environment variable AIT_SECRET_<CONNECTION_NAME>.
  2. The connection’s vault reference, akv://… or op://….
  3. The app’s secret store, when that store can be reached on this machine.

The variable name is the connection name in upper case, with every other character written as _. Users API becomes AIT_SECRET_USERS_API. gh-prod.v2 becomes AIT_SECRET_GH_PROD_V2.

item.title: Pipelines
item.description:
A pipeline builds termorq-cli, points it at the checkout with an absolute path, and passes each connection secret in from the forge’s secret store. The JUnit document is written to standard output. Warnings stay on standard error, so a skipped step does not corrupt the XML.

flowchart LR
 checkout[("Checkout\n.ai-terminal/")]:::store
 secrets[("Forge\nsecret store")]:::secret
 build["cargo build\n--bin termorq-cli"]:::step
 run["termorq-cli run\n--format junit"]:::run
 report(["Publish the XML\neven if the run fails"]):::out

 checkout --> build --> run
 secrets --> run
 run --> report

 classDef store fill:#134e4a,stroke:#5eead4,stroke-width:2px,color:#f4fbfa
 classDef secret fill:#FFC131,stroke:#b45309,stroke-width:2px,color:#1a1404
 classDef step fill:#155e75,stroke:#67e8f9,stroke-width:2px,color:#f4fbfa
 classDef run fill:#0f766e,stroke:#99f6e4,stroke-width:2px,color:#f4fbfa
 classDef out fill:#166534,stroke:#86efac,stroke-width:2px,color:#f0fdf4
 linkStyle 0,1 stroke:#5eead4,stroke-width:2.5px
 linkStyle 2 stroke:#FFC131,stroke-width:2.5px
 linkStyle 3 stroke:#86efac,stroke-width:2.5px

The commands below are the same ones in Run a collection. Swap Smoke and AIT_SECRET_USERS_API for your collection and connection. Add --allow-shell only when you have read the shell lines. Add --yes only when the plan calls a destructive tool.

item.title: Web Check
item.description:
Web Check is available in Pro builds. Free termorq-cli binaries do not include the termorq-cli web-check command.

Web Check runs saved API endpoints and MCP tools from a foreground termorq-cli process. Its local browser interface manages checks and displays SQLite-backed history. The header labels the build edition as FREE or PRO. Closing the browser keeps monitoring running. Ctrl+C or computer sleep interrupts it.

On Pro builds, use the Windows notification-area menu, the macOS menu-bar menu, or the macOS Dock menu to start or stop Web Check and show its output. The Show Web Check output option includes the local URL and pairing code. Windows Pro NSIS .exe and Microsoft Store MSIX packages include the matching termorq-cli.exe; macOS and other builds need termorq-cli beside the app or on PATH for Start Web Check to work. If the CLI is missing, the menu still appears and reports that when selected.
